JS SDK

JS SDK Introduction

JS SDK is a web development toolkit provided by Macle for web developers.

By using JS SDK, web developers can use Macle's capabilities of taking photos, scanning codes, and location systems efficiently. In addition, web developers can directly use Macle's unique capabilities to provide users with better web page experience.

Since web-view has not extended events, JS SDK supports only API invocation.

How to Use

According to different application scenarios, the usage can be classified into two types.

DSL Mini Program

  1. Web developers import the js-sdk.js file and use the interface provided by the JS SDK.

  2. Create an Mini Program and use the web-view container in the Mini Program.

  3. The web-view container link points to the H5 page of the page developer.

H5 Mini Program

  1. Web developers directly introduce js-sdk to the project and import related APIs to the source code.

  2. Use the Mini Program converter to convert the H5 project.

Version Number Identification (Minimum Version: 24.6.0)

In order to facilitate developers to distinguish different versions of JS-SDK, Macle adds a version number identification in the first line of the SDK file. The specific identification format is as follows:

/*Macle ${Macle_Version} jssdk ${NPM_Version} ${Date}*/

Tips:

  1. Some JS SDK APIs can be used only in DSL Mini Programs. For details, see Interface Description.
  2. Currently, when using the simulator for local debugging, online introduction of JSSDK for webview components is not supported.
